candidates.title: NWSA records decreased container volume September
candidates.excerpt: The Northwest Seaport Alliance recorded September 2026 total container volume of 265,692 TEUs, down 8.1% compared to September 2025, with full imports down 4.4% and full exports declining 9.6% year-on-year. However, on a month-on-month basis September delivered a significant sequential improvement, with full imports up 21.5% and full exports up 24.2% over August, indicating strengthening momentum heading into the final quarter of the year. Year-on-year declines continue to reflect the elevated 2025 baseline established when cargo was shipped ahead of anticipated tariff changes. Year-to-date through September, total volumes reached 2,174,231 TEUs, down 10.6 percent, with full imports declining 12.2% and full exports down 2.3%. Domestic container volumes decreased 0.3% year-to-date, with Alaska up 0.6% and Hawaii down 5 percent. candidates.title: Intra-Asia rates soften as congestion at major ports begins to ease
candidates.excerpt: Intra-Asia rates are receding from their recent highs as bottlenecks in major Chinese and other Asian ports subside. On 15 October, Drewry’s Intra-Asia Container Index dipped 3%, to an average of $1,453 per 40ft. Rates from Shanghai to key destinations, including Busan in South Korea, Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam, and Jawaharlal Nehru Port in India, softened as vessel waiting times declined. The Golden Week holiday in China also gave ports an opportunity to clear cargo backlogs, helping improve schedule reliability. Linerlytica calculated that North Asia now accounted for 37% of global port congestion, which is still the highest among all regions, but down from 50% last month. Rates from Shanghai to Nhava Sheva fell 11%, to $3,370 per 40ft, while those to Busan declined 8% to $1,000 per 40ft. Shanghai–Singapore rates dropped 7% to $1,973 per 40ft. candidates.title: Is the Red Sea safe?
candidates.excerpt: Is the Red Sea safe? An accelerating return of container shipping to the Suez Canal, Red Sea and Bab El Mandeb, amid an escalating and widening conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen-based Houthis is raising industry concerns. Are crew and cargoes at risk? For almost three years, since the latest conflict in the Middle East began, container shipping lines have diverted their vessels around the Cape of Good Hope. Some tentative attempts were made to return to the far shorter Red Sea route earlier this year, but the US war on Iran stalled the return to Suez Canal transits. Since the summer, however, an accelerated return to the far shorter route has seen some 63% of pre-war capacity return to the route which bisects North and East Africa to the west and Saudi Arabia and Yemen to the east. Increased tensions in the region, particularly between Saudi Arabia and Yemen-based Houthis, are again causing anxiety amongst industry organisations, except it seems the shipping lines. candidates.title: Union Pacific CFO to retire
candidates.excerpt: Chief Financial Officer Jennifer Hamann will retire in early 2027, Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) has announced. Hamann, who joined Union Pacific in 1992, was named CFO in January 2020. She had previously held leadership roles in a broad range of areas, including finance, human resources, marketing and sales, investor relations, and corporate audit. “For 35 years, she led with integrity and heart, guiding our finances through historic challenges, executing our strategy, mentoring future leaders and representing Union Pacific across the industry,” UP Chief Executive Jim Vena said in release. “Jennifer was tough — she never said yes unless she believed it was the right thing to do for Union Pacific. She made this railroad stronger, and her contributions will be felt for generations. I am deeply grateful for her leadership and friendship.” Hamann is the first woman to serve as the railroad’s chief financial officer. candidates.title: CSX profit jumps on volume and revenue growth
candidates.excerpt: JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — CSX’s third-quarter profits increased due to a combination of volume growth, higher fuel surcharge revenue, and efficiency gains, the railroad reported today (Oct. 21). Operating income increased 44%, to $1.57 billion, while revenue increased 12%, to a record $4.02 billion. Earnings per share increased 54%, to 57 cents. Adjusting for the impact of a one-time goodwill impairment in the third quarter of 2025, operating income was up 25% and earnings per share rose 30%. The railroad’s operating ratio was 60.9%, an 8.8-point improvement from a year ago, as expenses declined 2%. CSX set what it called an all-time U.S. quarterly record for fuel efficiency, at 0.92 gallons per 1,000 gross ton-miles. That included 232,120 carloads, up 3.5%, and 308,015 containers and trailers, an increase of 12.6%. For the year to date, overall volume is 21,062,681 carloads and intermodal units, a gain of 3.7% compared with the first 41 weeks of 2025. The 9,374,717 carloads represent a 2.7% increase, while the 11,687,964 intermodal units are an increase of 4.6%. North American figures for the week, from nine reporting U.S., Canadian, and Mexican railroads, show 731,715 carloads and intermodal units, a 7.2% increase over the corresponding week in 2025. candidates.title: BNSF route to El Paso closed by derailment
candidates.excerpt: LEASBURG, N.M. — BNSF Railway’s El Paso Subdivision is expected to remain closed until midday on Thursday following the Tuesday, Oct. 20, derailment of a train carrying flax seed. The derailment at Leasburg occurred about 5 a.m., BNSF said in a statement to Trains, and was due to extreme flooding in the region. There were no reported injuries and no hazardous materials involved. The railroad did not indicate the number of railcars involved. Officials in Doña Ana County said Doña Ana Road between Lujan Road and State Route 187 was expected to remain closed until Friday. Leasburg is approximately 11 miles north of Las Cruces, N.M., and 54 miles north of El Paso, Texas. — To report news or errors, contact trainsnewswire@firecrown.com.
